original_value: AbstractBackgroundA common yet still manual task in basic biology research, high-throughput drug screening and digital pathology is identifying the number, location, and type of individual cells in images. Object detection methods can be useful for identifying individual cells as well as their phenotype in one step. State-of-the-art deep learning for object detection is poised to improve the accuracy and efficiency of biological image analysis.ResultsWe createdKeras R-CNNto bring leading computational research to the everyday practice of bioimage analysts.Keras R-CNNimplements deep learning object detection techniques using Keras and Tensorflow (https://github.com/broadinstitute/keras-rcnn). We demonstrate the command line tool’s simplified Application Programming Interface on two important biological problems, nucleus detection and malaria stage classification, and show its potential for identifying and classifying a large number of cells. For malaria stage classification, we compare results with expert human annotators and find comparable performance.ConclusionsKeras R-CNNis a Python package that performs automated cell identification for both brightfield and fluorescence images and can process large image sets. Both the package and image datasets are freely available on GitHub and the Broad Bioimage Benchmark Collection.

result.paraphrase: AbstractBackground A common but still manual task in basic biology research, high-throughput drug screening, and digital pathology is determining the number, location, and type of individual cells in images. Object detection methods can help identify individual cells and their phenotype in a single step. State-of-the-art deep learning for object detection is set to improve the accuracy and efficiency of biological image analysis.Results We developed Keras R-CNN to bring leading computational research into the everyday practice of bioimage analysts. Keras R-CNN implements deep learning object detection techniques with Keras and TensorFlow (https://github.com/broadinstitute/keras-rcnn). We demonstrate the command-line tool’s streamlined Application Programming Interface on two key biological problems, nucleus detection and malaria stage classification, and show its potential for identifying and classifying large numbers of cells. For malaria stage classification, we compare results with expert human annotators and find comparable performance.Conclusions Keras R-CNN is a Python package for automated cell identification in both brightfield and fluorescence images, and it can process large image sets. Both the package and the image datasets are freely available on GitHub and in the Broad Bioimage Benchmark Collection.
